answer: Each identity tends one island juniper bush and locks an 80-credit bond to its jade seal. Each epoch it files height and berry weight. An auditor recomputes weight by height and age from the island juniper yield table and checks the jade seal serial. A record over 4 percent from the table, a reused serial, or a copied harvest burns the bond. The first identity pays 38; the kth from one source pays 38+6(k-1), so the 1000th pays 6032. One thousand fakes pay 3,035,000 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-bush ring fails: serial, height, and weight must match one bush. An honest grower pays 38 once.
